title: introduce-econ-autocalibrator-adaptive-prefill-guardrails
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers frequently need safe, automatic defaults for batching/prefill (prefix caching), and quantization profiles that respect a per-customer cost SLO. Manual tuning is time-consuming and error-prone, leading to regressions or overconservative defaults. This change introduces the 'econ-autocalibrator' subsystem: a simulation-backed suggestion engine that synthesizes safe batching/prefill/quant profiles given a workload fingerprint and a target unit-econ constraint. Key goals: 1) provide immediate out-of-the-box defaults that reduce token cost without violating latency SLOs; 2) offer a canary-safe rollout path (suggestions applied as config overlays with shadow simulation); 3) integrate telemetry and conservative safety checks to avoid regressions in quality or tail latency. The description below covers components, testing, rollout plan, and known limitations. Components: - service/econ-autocalibrator: main Go service implementing workload fingerprint ingestion, simulation runner (cost+latency model), and suggestion scoring with safety heuristics (max tail-latency multiplier, quality regression budget). - cli/bin/econctl: lightweight CLI to generate suggestions from local traces or stored workloads (used by SEs and SREs). - runtime integration: a new SuggestionConfig type, plus an adapter in the routing layer to apply suggested overrides as staged config (shadow, canary, apply). - default profiles: curated prefill/batch/quant presets generated by the simulator and validated against common benchmarks. - telemetry: metrics for suggestion accept rate, simulated vs. actual delta, suggestion age, and safety violations. Checklist (all items in this single paragraph per repo conventions): - [x] design doc: ENG-4187 linked - [x] unit tests for scoring and safety heuristics - [x] end-to-end integration test in perf-canary harness - [x] docs: console and CLI usage - [x] migration: SuggestionConfig is additive and defaults to no-op - [x] observability: add tracing spans and metrics - [x] canary rollout plan documented. Limitations and future work: current simulator uses a conservative latency model; quantization acceptance checks are heuristic and will be replaced by a lightweight regression eval in a follow-up; policy zoning for tenant-level hard caps needs product alignment. Usage notes: operators can run econctl against traces or request suggestions via the Console UI (new 'Econ suggestions' card). Suggestions are returned with a confidence score and a recommended rollout policy (shadow -> canary -> apply).
